question: Where can asymmetry occur when every immediate neighborhood is the same matching?
inputs: Previously supplied SRGs are accepted; no duplicate computation of their full automorphism groups

definitions.transport_graph: T_x has vertex set F_x and edge yz exactly when yz is an edge of G whose unique triangle has its third vertex in N(x)
definitions.rooted_skeleton: K_x retains all edges touching N[x], plus all T_x edges; x is distinguished
definitions.residual_graph: U_x=G[F_x] minus the edges of T_x

proved_from_lambda_one: For each y in F_x and each a in N(x) intersect N(y), the triangle through ay has third vertex z in F_x. Otherwise x and y would both complete an edge inside N(x).
Distinct a give distinct z, because otherwise the edge yz would lie in two triangles. Hence T_x is mu-regular.
No T_x edge can lie in a triangle wholly in F_x: it already has its unique triangle completed in N(x). Therefore T_x is triangle-free, and every triangle of G[F_x] lies wholly in U_x.
G[F_x] is (k-mu)-regular. Thus U_x is (k-2mu)-regular, and every edge of U_x lies in exactly one triangle of U_x.
For mu=2, T_x is a disjoint union of cycles of length at least four. Their lengths form an intrinsic vertex invariant, despite the constant immediate matching neighborhoods.
An automorphism of G fixing x induces an automorphism of the rooted K_x. Thus Aut(G)_x is a subgroup of Aut(K_x,x).

If the intrinsic color class of x has size m and Aut(K_x,x) has order h, then |Aut(G)| <= m*h by orbit-stabilizer. In particular, a unique intrinsic root with a rigid rooted skeleton proves full asymmetry.

interpretation: A nontrivial point stabilizer is not forced by lambda=1, even with mu=2: the gamma6 and gamma8 examples contain intrinsically described rigid rooted skeletons.
Root rigidity and distinguishability of the root are separate requirements. Known symmetries may survive entirely by moving a rigid root to other globally equivalent roots.
These observations supply an asymmetry criterion, not a construction of a new asymmetric SRG and not a nonexistence argument for Conway.
empirical_question_not_a_theorem: CORRECTION: all cycles in the eight stored243 examples are even, but not all are divisible by4: twin243 has length30 cycles. The partial99 example with cycles4,11,69 shows only that evenness is not forced by the stated local constraints; its global completability remains unknown.

transition_system_mu_two.base_graph: H=K_k minus the matching P induced by N(x)
transition_system_mu_two.far_vertices: Exactly one far vertex for every nonmatched pair {a,b} of N(x); this follows from mu=2.
transition_system_mu_two.transitions: The triangles through a in N(x) pair the H-edges incident with a. Transport cycles are the circuits of this transition system.
transition_system_mu_two.group_description: Aut(K_x,x) is exactly the group of permutations of N(x) preserving P and the unoriented collection of circuit words. Consecutive letters encode each far vertex.
transition_system_mu_two.finite_certificate: A circuit whose length L occurs once and whose word uses all k letters determines each rooted automorphism by one of at most 2L dihedral alignments. Repeated letters, P, and the remaining circuit words filter those alignments.
transition_system_mu_two.gamma6: The unique length68 circuit at root0 spans all22 letters. Equality of repeated letters alone rejects all135 nonidentity dihedral alignments.
transition_system_mu_two.gamma8: The unique length40 circuit at root0 spans all22 letters. Equality of repeated letters alone rejects all79 nonidentity alignments.
transition_system_mu_two.meaning: Rooted rigidity can already be encoded in one circuit; no full graph automorphism calculation is required.

local_cycle_divisibility_counterexample.status: PARTIAL graph only; not an SRG and no claim of global completability
local_cycle_divisibility_counterexample.satisfied: Closed-star rows complete; present edges have exactly one common neighbor; nonedges have at most two.
local_cycle_divisibility_counterexample.conclusion: Evenness is not forced by these local constraints alone. Divisibility by four is already false in the complete twin243 graph, which has cycles of length30.

fixed_skeleton_completion_corollary.hypothesis: Let m count roots of the SEED with the same invariant of K_x itself (here the unrefined T_x invariant), h=|Aut(K_x,x)|, and suppose accepted |Aut(G)|=m*h.
fixed_skeleton_completion_corollary.conclusion: A different labelled SRG completion with exactly the same rooted skeleton K_x cannot be isomorphic to the seed G.
fixed_skeleton_completion_corollary.proof: The orbit of x has at least |Aut(G)|/h=m points and lies in the m-class, so equals it; the point stabilizer has size h. Thus all rooted skeleton isomorphisms from K_x to a compatible K_y are restrictions of actual automorphisms of G. The skeleton has the entire vertex set. An isomorphism of another completion to G would therefore also be an automorphism of G, forcing that completion to equal G.
fixed_skeleton_completion_corollary.application: The computed bounds are saturated for Gamma5-8 and hemi378, using the full group orders already supplied by the peer. Hence a search keeping their rooted skeletons may block the one labelled seed without separately enumerating isomorphic copies.
fixed_skeleton_completion_corollary.limit: A different completion would be a new isomorphism class, but not automatically asymmetric. No such completion has been constructed.

completion_uniqueness_status: Not proved for Gamma6 or Gamma8. Root rigidity and saturation of the local automorphism bound do not imply uniqueness of completion. See skeleton_completion_theory.json.
